# ThrottleDeck Broker: detailed machine-readable context

## Purpose

ThrottleDeck Broker is the one local owner of shared Polymarket US and Kalshi read
budgets. Multiple bots share one public IP; independent per-process limiters can
collectively exceed a venue ceiling even when each bot looks healthy. Every
adopted caller sends reads through this service with an `X-Broker-Caller` label.

The broker binds to `127.0.0.1:8777`, accepts only GET, performs explicit caching
and single-flight coalescing, schedules callers through weighted classes, and
admits upstream work through one budget per venue product. A missing broker is a
hard failure: `broker_client.py` raises `BrokerUnavailableError` and never falls
back to a direct venue read.

## Active routing and budgets

- `/pmus/<path>` routes public Polymarket US reads to
  `https://gateway.polymarket.us/<path>`.
- Retail `/v1/account`, `/v1/portfolio`, and `/v1/orders` reads route to
  `https://api.polymarket.us/<path>`.
- `/kalshi/<path>` routes prediction-market reads relative to Kalshi's
  `/trade-api/v2` base.
- Kalshi margin/perps reads use a separate weighted limiter and require an
  explicitly configured perps read rate.
- A fresh install uses the Kalshi Basic prediction tier with the documented
  safety margin: 180 tokens/second refill and 360-token capacity. Perps remain
  disabled until their documented account rate is explicitly configured.
- Polymarket US uses 18 requests/second and an 18-request rolling-second ceiling.

Query strings and caller authentication headers pass through unchanged in
memory. Authentication material is never logged, cached raw, or persisted.
Unknown paths are not cached. See `README.md` and `venue_broker/config.py` for
the complete weighted-cost and TTL tables.

## Failure contract

Venue responses preserve their status and body and carry
`X-Venue-Broker-Source: venue`. Locally generated failures carry structured JSON
and `X-Venue-Broker-Source: broker`. Important local outcomes include upstream
timeout 504, upstream connection failure 502, broker closing 503, oversized
weighted request 400, invalid batch cost 400, unconfigured perps budget 503,
stopped broker access 423, and unavailable control state 503.

ThrottleDeck Broker's `/health` and `/metrics` endpoints are cheap local reads that do not
consume venue capacity. A venue outage does not make `/health` fail and must not
trigger a supervisor restart loop.

## ThrottleDeck control window

ThrottleDeck uses a separate per-user control plane on `127.0.0.1:8778`. It serves a
React dashboard and authenticated same-origin control API; it never proxies venue
traffic and never starts, stops, or restarts ThrottleDeck Broker. Durable state, sampled
history, rollups, maintenance, and the audit log live under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ThrottleDeck`.

The standalone Edge app opens at 940 by 700 pixels and remains freely resizable.
Its visual system is cool near-black with graphite surfaces, cool-gray separators,
iOS-style blue interaction accents, and semantic green, amber, and red. The
startup viewport keeps complete budget details while application rows use a
concise two-line form and Control activity starts collapsed to one priority row.
The approximately 920 by 650 usable content area inside the 940 by 700 Windows
frame is regression-tested for zero page overflow. It is also tested at 720 by
480.

Application-row traffic is measured brokered REST, not total bot activity. Each
row exposes the exact recent count/window, the last brokered-REST request age,
and adjacent-sample request deltas as a sparkline. Missing or reset intervals are
null gaps, not zeroes. Direct requests and WebSocket streams are explicitly
outside Governor's measurement; the UI never claims those streams are active or
idle.

Expanded application details expose a per-venue recent request split, upstream
429 count, 429s seen while the broker retained headroom, and worst broker queue
wait. The manual authenticated `POST /api/v1/diagnostics/direct-egress` endpoint
samples established Windows HTTPS connections only when an operator asks. It
returns process name, PID, venue, and observation count; it never accepts or
returns command lines or request material. A clear sample is not proof that no
bypass exists, because short-lived connections can be missed.

Both broker collection and dashboard polling use a one-miss grace period. One
transient automatic miss preserves the last fresh sample without flashing an
outage. Two consecutive misses show the warning. An older failed poll cannot
overwrite a newer successful manual refresh.

Five-second samples retain 6 hours and minute rollups retain 90 days. The 250 MB
guard pauses history writes only, not controls. Recovery maintenance compacts the
database only after a guard pause and eligible rollup, checkpoints the WAL again,
then resumes collection if total database, WAL, and SHM storage is below the cap.

Control mutations are never optimistic. The old state remains visible until the
service returns a committed revision, and a revision conflict reloads the
authoritative snapshot. Broker-access controls affect brokered REST reads only;
they do not stop processes, direct reads, or WebSockets. The configured new-money
control does not cancel or flatten existing orders.

Application IDs, display names, exact caller groups, paper/real-money labels,
coverage notes, and the protected application are loaded from the operator's
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ThrottleDeck\apps.toml`. A neutral fallback ships as
`governor/default-apps.toml`, and the shortcut installer copies it only when the
per-user file does not already exist. Caller labels must be unique. Restart both
ThrottleDeck and ThrottleDeck Broker after a registry change so observation and
broker-access policy use the same mapping. Configuration files, fixtures, docs,
and screenshots must not expose an operator's private application names.

The per-install control key stays in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ThrottleDeck\control.key`, is
sent only in memory, and never appears in a command line or log. A one-use launch
nonce becomes an HttpOnly same-origin browser session.

## Windows operation

For a fresh Windows checkout, open elevated PowerShell and run
`powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\setup-throttledeck.ps1`.
The idempotent setup checks Windows, Python 3.12, Edge, administrator rights, and
the local broker/control ports; creates `.venv` only when absent; installs runtime
dependencies; registers the one broker task; preserves any existing per-user app
configuration; creates the desktop shortcut; starts the control window hidden;
and waits for both local health endpoints. It neither requests nor persists
exchange account material. Add `-PreflightOnly` to validate the prerequisites
without changing the machine.

`scripts/install-broker-task.ps1` remains the one scheduled-task installer. Do
not invent or launch a second broker instance. Governor has one desktop shortcut
installed by `scripts/install-governor-shortcut.ps1`; its VBS and PowerShell
launchers keep consoles hidden, start Governor only when its local health endpoint
is absent, and open Microsoft Edge in app mode.

## Safe development workflow

Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and the cited official venue documentation before
changing service behavior. Never probe a live venue merely to infer an API shape
that the venue already documents.

Python verification:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\pytest.exe -q
.\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe check .
```

Governor UI verification:

```powershell
npm --prefix ui test
npm --prefix ui run typecheck
npm --prefix ui run build
npm --prefix ui run test:e2e
```

The UI build writes committed assets to `governor/static/`. Browser tests
intercept every API request and call no venue. Changes near broker access or the
configured money lock require tests proving they cannot self-enable unsafe state.
